mechanisms.problemSolved: Model hallucinates component names, prop shapes, and import paths when a component library is only known from training data.
mechanisms.mechanism: A short static SKILL.md ships alongside the registry, listing every component's exact props, exact file path, and an explicit anti-pattern ('always import from the exact file, never a barrel'). No design opinions are encoded, only API ground truth.
mechanisms.whyItWorks: It answers a factual question (what does this API look like) rather than a judgement question (what should this look like), so it removes a class of hallucination without moving a design decision out of the model.
mechanisms.outputImpact: Reduces broken imports/props when generating code against a real component library; no effect on visual/design quality.
failureModes: Goes stale if the registry changes and the reference doc isn't regenerated alongside it — no verification harness ties the two together in this repo.
mechanisms.testMethod: Generate code against the registry with and without the reference doc loaded; count import/prop errors.
mechanisms.sitesmithForm: If SiteSmith ever bundles or references a fixed component set (e.g. shadcn primitives), ship a short, regenerated-on-change reference of exact paths/props rather than relying on the model's training-data memory of the library.

mechanisms.problemSolved: Rendering an AI agent's own tool calls (Bash, Edit, Search, Plan, Subagent, MCP) inside a chat transcript.
mechanisms.mechanism: 26 pre-built React components (AgentChat, MessageList, InputBar, tool cards) installed via shadcn CLI from a hosted registry.
mechanisms.whyItWorks: n/a — not applicable to the target problem.
mechanisms.outputImpact: None for an ordinary website; only relevant to a site that itself embeds an agent/chat interface.
failureModes: Becoming a default dependency of every SiteSmith build regardless of whether the site has a chat interface, per the task's explicit constraint.
conflicts: Any site with no agent/chat surface — the components have nothing to render.
mechanisms.sitesmithForm: Not a default dependency. At most, note as an option only when the brief explicitly calls for an embedded agent/chat UI.

mechanisms.problemSolved: A body of knowledge too large to load in full needs to be reachable without bloating every invocation.
mechanisms.mechanism: One short SKILL.md (48 lines) containing a one-paragraph-per-topic table of contents, each entry a relative markdown link to that topic's own entry file, loaded by the model only when the topic is relevant.
mechanisms.whyItWorks: Keeps the always-loaded surface tiny (a table of contents, not the content) while making the full breadth reachable on demand — this is the same shape as the 55-line frontend-design file that beat SiteSmith's 630k-token package: small root, expand only on need.
mechanisms.outputImpact: Keeps unrelated topics out of context; model self-selects only the relevant slice.
failureModes: Router entries can go stale if a linked file moves and the link isn't updated — mitigated here by validate-links.ts, not by the router format itself.
mechanisms.testMethod: Run a link-validation script (see scripts/validate-links.ts) as part of CI; confirm every router entry resolves.
mechanisms.sitesmithForm: SiteSmith's own SKILL.md should stay a short entry point that links out to on-demand reference files for specialized topics, rather than inlining everything — this is already the direction implied by the 500-line cap; treat the cap as a router-file discipline, not just a size limit.

mechanisms.problemSolved: Multiple mutually-exclusive implementation techniques for the same feature (four different mapping libraries) need to be presented without forcing the model to load all four.
mechanisms.mechanism: Explicit instruction (paraphrased; licence forbids quoting this source) to select a single mapping technique matching the intended shot and load only that technique's own doc, with a stated design invariant that each technique directory is self-contained and removable without breaking the others.
mechanisms.whyItWorks: Turns a menu of alternatives into a genuine one-of-N choice for the model to make, rather than a script pre-selecting for it — this is a 'help the model think better' mechanism, not a lookup-table shortcut, because the model still makes the choice using judgement about the brief (need 3D flyover vs free/no-API-key vs nicest default styling).
requiredContext: one REFERENCE.md (~37 lines) + one chosen TECHNIQUE.md
mechanisms.outputImpact: Prevents loading 4x the content when only one technique is ever used per task.
failureModes: None specific to this mechanism; risk shifts to whether technique docs are actually independent, which the source states as a hard constraint.
mechanisms.testMethod: Delete one technique directory; confirm the others still resolve and load correctly.
mechanisms.sitesmithForm: For any SiteSmith reference topic with several mutually exclusive implementation paths (e.g. animation library choice, CMS integration choice), use the same 'pick exactly one, load only that one, each option removable independently' framing instead of one file trying to cover all options.

mechanisms.problemSolved: A sub-skill (e.g. remotion-maps) needs to be reachable both as its own standalone, independently publishable skill and nested inside a router skill's directory, without the harness auto-discovering and double-registering it as a top-level skill.
mechanisms.mechanism: A dev-time script symlinks each sub-skill folder into the parent skill's directory; a publish-time script renames the embedded copy's SKILL.md to REFERENCE.md and rewrites its internal relative links so the harness doesn't see two competing top-level skills with the same name.
mechanisms.whyItWorks: It solves a real problem, but only the problem a multi-skill monorepo has. Verified with git ls-tree that what actually ships is physical duplicate trees (mode 040000, not 120000 symlinks); a repo-wide md5sum pass found 83 files sharing 62 unique hashes, i.e. ~25% of the tree is duplicate bytes of content that exists elsewhere in the same tree. A --check mode exists specifically to catch drift between the copies, which is itself evidence that drift is an anticipated, real failure mode, not a hypothetical one.
mechanisms.outputImpact: None on generation quality; this is packaging/build tooling, not content the model reads to build better output.
failureModes: Drift between the canonical and embedded copies if the sync script is skipped
Triple-copy nesting when a sub-skill is embedded inside a skill that is itself embedded (remotion-maps appears 3 times in this checkout)
conflicts: SiteSmith is being rebuilt as ONE skill; the problem this machinery solves (one sub-skill needing to live inside multiple parent skills without double-registration) does not exist for a single-skill package.
mechanisms.sitesmithForm: Do not adopt the symlink+rename+duplicate build pipeline. The router idea (mechanism above) is separable from this machinery and is the only part worth keeping.

mechanisms.problemSolved: Backward compatibility for old MCP configs after the underlying service moved from a standalone Magic MCP server to a unified, paid, hosted 21st MCP endpoint.
mechanisms.mechanism: A ~220-line stdio-to-HTTP relay: reads JSON-RPC lines from stdin, POSTs each to https://21st.dev/api/mcp with an API key header, returns the response. No component data, generation logic, or registry exists in this repository — it is entirely behind the hosted endpoint.
mechanisms.whyItWorks: n/a — there is no mechanism here to evaluate for SiteSmith's purposes; the actual capability being proxied to is invisible to this autopsy.
requiredContext: a paid API key from a third-party console
mechanisms.outputImpact: None observable from this repo; any component-generation quality lives entirely on a remote paid service this task cannot inspect.
failureModes: Total dependency on a third-party paid service with no local fallback
Latches into a permanent failure state after one 401 (src/index.ts:108-116), so a stale/reset key silently stops working for the rest of the session
conflicts: Any offline, license-clean, redistributable design principle.
mechanisms.sitesmithForm: No role in SiteSmith. Nothing to adapt — the repository contains a network shim, not a mechanism.

mechanisms.problemSolved: Making an unverified external dependency sound credible to a non-technical user during onboarding.
mechanisms.mechanism: Specific, precise-sounding counts of design styles, color palettes, font pairings, and pre-built components (paraphrased; licence forbids quoting this source) asserted as scripted dialogue for the model to say, with no underlying data in this repository to back them — they describe external npm/API dependencies (uipro-cli, 21st.dev Magic) this repo does not contain.
mechanisms.whyItWorks: It doesn't work in the sense the task cares about — it's marketing copy for the human, not a mechanism that improves model output. It is exactly the kind of 'lookup table' framing (a large fixed catalog implicitly presented as the source of good taste) that the frontend-design vs SiteSmith result argues against: a big fixed catalog is not what won.
requiredContext: none — the numbers are asserted, not backed by inspectable data
mechanisms.outputImpact: Unverifiable; likely negative if it substitutes for actual design reasoning by treating a fixed external palette/component list as sufficient.
failureModes: Convergent output across unrelated projects, since many installs draw from the identical closed catalog — the same failure class as SiteSmith's own 0/8 showcase problem, potentially worse because it's shared across every user of this skill, not just within one project.
conflicts: Both measured facts in the brief: it is a lookup-table mechanism, and a shared fixed catalog is a house-style-convergence liability.
mechanisms.testMethod: n/a — no data in-repo to test
mechanisms.sitesmithForm: No role. If SiteSmith ever needs credibility-building onboarding copy, it should describe what the model actually reasons over (heuristics, principles), not a fixed catalog size.

mechanisms.problemSolved: A multi-step external-dependency install flow needs to survive individual step failures without stalling the whole task.
mechanisms.mechanism: Explicit rules: walk through steps one at a time, never dump all instructions at once, and on any install failure acknowledge it, give the manual fallback command, and keep moving rather than halting.
mechanisms.whyItWorks: Generic UX resilience pattern for scripted multi-step flows with real side effects (global npm installs, editing ~/.claude.json); not specific to website building.
requiredContext: a multi-step setup flow with side effects to narrate
mechanisms.outputImpact: Affects onboarding UX only, not site-generation output quality.
failureModes: None specific; this is the least risky part of the source.
mechanisms.testMethod: n/a — no analogous flow currently exists in SiteSmith to test against.
mechanisms.sitesmithForm: SiteSmith has no comparable multi-step external-install flow today; nothing to attach this to. Revisit only if such a flow is added later.
